Author: Prashant Kumar Mishra
Bench: Prashant Kumar Mishra
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. /2026
 (Arising out of Slp (Crl.) No(s). 13001/20
 Shatrunjai Pundir P
 Versus
 State Of Uttarakhand & Anr. R
 O R D E R

1. Leave granted.
2.

This appeal arises out of an order passed by the High Court refusing to quash charges under Sections 498A, 323 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 arising out of the FIR No. 106 of 2022 registered with Police Station Raipur, District Dehradun against the appellant.
3. During the pendency of this appeal, the parties were referred to mediation vide order dated 16.10.2025 and the same has become fruitful.

4. The settlement arrived at between the parties is recorder by the Mediation Centre by way of a Settlement Agreement dated 18.12.2025, which is duly signed by the respective parties, their counsel and the Mediator as well.
moved an application under Article-142 of the Constitution of India for recording the settlement and passing appropriate orders in terms thereof.

6. The Settlement Agreement dated 18.12.2025, records the following terms:
I. The Petitionerhusband shall pay first installment an amount of Rs. 10,00,000/-
(Rupees Ten Lakhs only) in favour of the Respondent No.2/ wife through RTGS/NEFT/IMPS on or before 20th December 2025.
II. The Petitionerhusband shall pay the remaining amount of Rs. 25,00,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs only) in favour of the Respondent No.2/ wife through Shatrunjai Pundir vs State Of Uttarakhand on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192156918/
1 RTGS/NEFT/ IMPS on or before 15th of January 2026.
III.

sentences.text: The parties agreed that the total amount shall be transferred by Petitioners father through his Bank Account for an on behalf of the Petitioner Husband.
7. It is submitted that the appellant has paid Rs.35,00,000/- to the respondent No.2/wife, as mentioned in the settlement agreement.
8. Besides the above, the parties have agreed to withdraw/close/quash the following cases:

( i ) xx xx xx (ii) Respondent No.2/wife has filed Criminal Case No. 7459/2022 pending before 6th Additional CJM, Dehradun-Uttarakhand arising out of FIR No. 106/2022 dated 28.02.2022 P.S. Raipur,
Dehradun-Uttarakhand.

(iii) Respondent No/2/wife has filed DV Case No. 1879 of 2021 which is pending before ACJ - 1,
Dehradun-Uttarakhand.
(iv) Respondent No/2 wife has filed Maintenance Case No. 34/2023 pending before Additional Family Court at Dehradun-Uttarakhand.

9. In view of the above settlement, we deem it appropriate to invoke our power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and order for dissolution of marriage between the parties which was solemnized on 07.10.2019 and has been irretrievably broken down.
10. The decree of divorce be drawn up accordingly.
11. The application (I.A. No. 21153/2026) stands disposed of in terms of the above with the expectation that the parties will act in terms of the settlement agreement dated 18.12.2025.
12. The appeal stands disposed of, accordingly.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
